en.title: Matt Damon Reveals Why Christopher Nolan Avoids Deleted Scenes
en.summary: Christopher Nolan's latest epic, 'The Odyssey,' is making waves with its home release. Amidst the buzz, star Matt Damon shed light on the director's unique approach to his films, particularly his stance on deleted scenes.
en.body:
Christopher Nolan's ambitious adaptation of Homer's epic, **The Odyssey**, has captivated audiences and is now sailing onto home release platforms, including Premium VOD, 4K, and DVD. With the film set for a special IMAX 70mm theatrical rerelease on December 11, the stars are aligning for another deep dive into this cinematic journey. To mark the occasion, Collider's Steve Weintraub sat down with **Matt Damon**, a key figure in the film's ensemble, who shared some fascinating insights into the mind of director **Christopher Nolan**.

When it comes to **Nolan**'s filmmaking, every element is carefully considered, from his preference for practical effects to his unwavering focus on narrative cohesion. This meticulousness extends to his approach to the final cut of his films. Unlike many directors who might offer audiences a glimpse of what didn't make the final edit, **Nolan** famously keeps his deleted scenes under wraps. **Matt Damon** offered a window into this directorial philosophy, suggesting that **Nolan**'s commitment to the story's integrity is paramount.

## Nolan's Unseen Cuts

During the conversation, **Damon** touched upon **Nolan**'s general approach to filmmaking, which prioritizes a streamlined and impactful narrative. While specific details about deleted scenes from **The Odyssey** were not elaborated upon, the implication from **Damon**'s comments aligns with **Nolan**'s known directorial style: a singular vision where every scene serves a purpose. **Nolan** has previously emphasized the importance of endings in his films, stating he needs to know the conclusion before he begins. This suggests a process where material is carefully curated, ensuring that what reaches the audience is the most potent and complete version of his story, leaving little room for extraneous material that might dilute its impact. The decision to withhold deleted scenes, therefore, seems less about hiding content and more about preserving the intended artistic statement.

## Fan Anticipation and Theories

For fans of **Christopher Nolan**, this approach fuels a particular kind of anticipation. The dedication to a perfect final product means that every frame we see on screen has been rigorously vetted. This exclusivity of the final cut only adds to the mystique surrounding his films, prompting discussions and theories about what might have been. **The Odyssey** is no exception, with its vast scope and star-studded cast already generating immense buzz. The fact that **Nolan** doesn't release deleted scenes means that the versions of the story we experience in theaters and at home are precisely as he intended them to be, a testament to his control over his artistic output. This practice, while perhaps frustrating for those eager for more content, underscores **Nolan**'s reputation as a filmmaker who delivers a singular, polished vision.

## What's Next

**The Odyssey** is currently available on Premium VOD, 4K, and DVD. Its theatrical rerelease in IMAX 70mm is scheduled for December 11. Fans eager to experience **Nolan**'s vision will have another opportunity to see the film on the grandest scale possible.

This Oscar contender is now available on Premium VOD, 4K, and DVD , ahead of its rerelease into theaters in IMAX 70mm on December 11, and in honor of this next journey, Collider’s Steve Weintraub had the opportunity to sit down and talk with stars Matt Damon and John Leguizamo .
